topic: DUAL MEMORY architectures for AI agents (2025-2026)

findings.title: Dual-Layer Agentic Memory with Fast Write Routing and Slow Consolidation
findings.key_findings: Proposes a dual-layer knowledge lifecycle system unifying external memory, parametric memory, fast write routing, and slow consolidation, directly inspired by Complementary Learning Systems (CLS) theory. Implements an operational memory taxonomy (non-write, write-new, write-update) with a cost-aware small-to-large model cascade for routing decisions. The 1.7B/8B cascade prunes up to 68% of redundant external memory while escalating fewer than 50% of inputs, yet retains over 98% of downstream QA Exact Match. Periodic write-back consolidation internalizes external knowledge into model parameters via supervised fine-tuning, allowing the router to adaptively suppress redundant writes as parametric knowledge evolves.

findings.title: Complementary Learning Systems Theory Updated (Kumaran, Hassabis, McClelland)
findings.venue: Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 2016 (cited as foundational in 2025-2026 agent memory papers)
findings.key_findings: Updates CLS theory showing recurrent activation of hippocampal traces can support generalization and neocortical learning can be rapid for information consistent with known structure. This neuroscience foundation underpins virtually all dual-memory AI agent architectures in 2025-2026, mapping hippocampal fast learning to external/episodic memory and neocortical slow consolidation to parametric/semantic memory.

findings.title: Human-Inspired Memory Architecture for LLM Agents
findings.key_findings: Biologically-grounded architecture with six cognitive mechanisms: sleep-phase consolidation, interference-based forgetting, engram maturation, reconsolidation on retrieval, entity knowledge graphs, and hybrid multi-cue retrieval. Maps three biological memory tiers to system components: short-term (prefrontal cortex → hot cache), medium-term (hippocampus → warm episodic store), long-term (neocortex → semantic knowledge graph). Introduces synthetic calibration methodology deriving all thresholds from LLM-generated corpora without benchmark exposure. On LongMemEval M-tier (475 sessions, ~540K turns), matches raw retrieval accuracy at 200K-token budget while exposing tunable accuracy/store-size curve; +13.3 pp improvement on S-tier preference recall.

findings.title: DG-Mem: Dual-Grained Agent Memory and Shapley Context Attribution for Multimodal Agentic Learner
findings.key_findings: Proposes dual-grained memory factoring into instance-grounded exemplar memory and category-level schema memory of IF-THEN rules, with a transient reflection store mediating consolidation (schemas synthesized exclusively from abstract reflections, never exemplar text). Two key innovations: (1) online concept categorizer growing category space incrementally during training, and (2) Shapley context attribution treating co-retrieved rules as players in a cooperative game to compute per-rule utility that re-weights retrieval at test time. Gradient-free pipeline deployable on closed-weight/on-device models. Improves consistently over baselines on MathVista, MMMU, MMMU-Pro across Qwen3.5-27B/122B, GPT-5-Nano, Gemini-3-Flash.

findings.title: SYNAPSE: Empowering LLM Agents with Episodic-Semantic Memory via Spreading Activation
findings.key_findings: Unified Episodic-Semantic Graph where raw interaction logs (episodic nodes) are synthesized into abstract concepts (semantic nodes). Retrieval governed by spreading activation dynamics: input signals inject energy propagating through temporal and causal edges, with lateral inhibition suppressing distractors. Triple Hybrid Retrieval fuses semantic similarity (λ=0.5), activation-based traversal (λ=0.3), and structural PageRank (λ=0.2). On LoCoMo: +7.2 F1 over SOTA, 23% improvement on multi-hop reasoning, 95% token reduction vs full-context. Dynamic graph enables recovery from poor initial seeds via activation propagation.

findings.title: HeLa-Mem: Hebbian Learning and Associative Memory for LLM Agents
findings.key_findings: Bio-inspired dual-graph architecture: (1) Episodic Memory Graph evolves via Hebbian co-activation ('neurons that fire together wire together'), and (2) Semantic Memory Store populated via Hebbian Distillation — a Reflective Agent identifies densely-connected hubs and distills them into reusable semantic knowledge. Dual-Path Retrieval combines base semantic similarity path with spreading-augmented path traversing Hebbian edges. Achieves best average rank (1.25) across LoCoMo categories, 65.4% ACC vs A-MEM 62.6%, FullText 56.8%, Mem0 53.6%. Superior on Temporal (50.38%), Multi-Session (57.14%), Knowledge-Update (78.21%) reasoning.

findings.title: CraniMem: Cranial Inspired Gated and Bounded Memory for Agentic Systems
findings.key_findings: Dual-store architecture: bounded episodic buffer (FIFO, high-fidelity short-range continuity) + structured knowledge graph (long-term semantic recall). RAS-inspired gating module filters candidate writes with utility tagging (Importance + Surprise + Emotion). Scheduled consolidation loop replays high-utility traces into graph while pruning low-utility items. On HotpotQA with injected noise: CraniMem F1 0.312 vs Mem0 0.198 vs Vanilla RAG 0.068; smallest noise drop (0.011 vs Mem0 0.036). Beats Mem0 by +57.6% on noisy HotpotQA.

findings.title: D-Mem: A Dual-Process Memory System for LLM Agents
findings.key_findings: Dual-process architecture: System 1 (Mem0*) = fast vector retrieval for routine queries; System 2 (Full Deliberation) = exhaustive raw dialogue history processing for deep reasoning. Multi-dimensional Quality Gating evaluates System 1 output on Relevance, Faithfulness & Consistency, Completeness — escalates to System 2 only on failure. On LoCoMo with GPT-4o-mini: Quality Gating F1 53.5 vs Mem0* 51.2, recovers 96.7% of Full Deliberation performance (55.3) with significantly lower compute. Addresses 'lossy abstraction' of incremental compression and 'Lost-in-the-Middle' via query-guided chunk-by-chunk processing in System 2.

findings.title: Unified Memory Agent (UMA): End-to-End RL for Memory Operations
findings.key_findings: End-to-end RL framework unifying memory operations (create, update, delete, reorganize) and task execution in a single policy. Dual memory representation: compact core summary (global context) + structured Memory Bank (key-value CRUD). Task-Stratified GRPO with nested trajectory sampling (N memory rollouts × M query rollouts). Ledger-QA benchmark for continuous state tracking. UMA substantially outperforms long-context/RAG baselines on dynamic reasoning (72.98% avg on Ledger-QA vs 31.59% RAG, 43.47% MemAgent) while competitive on standard retrieval. Memory-R1, Mem-α, UMEM, MemFactory are related unified RL memory frameworks from 2026.

findings.title: Agentic Memory (AgeMem): Unified LTM/STM Management via RL
findings.key_findings: Unified framework integrating LTM and STM management into agent policy. Exposes memory ops as tool-based actions (store, retrieve, update, summarize, discard). Three-stage progressive RL with step-wise GRPO addressing sparse/discontinuous rewards from memory operations. Outperforms memory-augmented baselines on five long-horizon benchmarks across multiple LLM backbones.

findings.title: Towards Self-Evolving Agents: A Dual-Process Framework for Continual Context Refinement
findings.key_findings: System 1 = fast pattern matching (finite-state machine / small model); System 2 = deliberate meta-cognition (LLM with Theory of Mind). Dual-process at interaction level: System 1 produces default response, System 2 refines via reflective monitoring. Dual-process at memory level: System 1 = rapid episodic encoding; System 2 = slow semantic consolidation. Connects to SOAR/ACT-R cognitive architectures. Hierarchical memory for high-efficiency long-term reasoning (Sun & Zeng, 2025).

findings.title: Episodic Memory is the Missing Piece for Long-Term LLM Agents
findings.venue: ArXiv:2502.06975 (2025 position paper, cited in 2026 works)
findings.key_findings: Defines five properties episodic memory must have: long-term storage, explicit reasoning, single-shot learning, instance-specific memories, contextual memories (who, when, where, why). Argues current agents implement only hippocampal exemplar storage (fast) without neocortical weight consolidation (slow) — the CLS gap. Episodic memory enables history, not just knowledge; semantic memory tells what is generally true; procedural memory tells how to behave.

findings.title: Memory for Autonomous LLM Agents: Mechanisms, Evaluation, and Open Problems
findings.key_findings: Survey identifying dual-buffer consolidation as promising approach: new memories in 'hot' buffer during probation, promoted to long-term only after quality checks (re-verification, deduplication, importance scoring). Mirrors hippocampal-to-neocortical transfer. Catalogs 2025-2026 wave: Agentic Memory [Yu et al., 2026] (unified STM/LTM policy via step-wise GRPO), MemBench [Tan et al., 2025], MemoryAgentBench [Hu et al., 2025] (tests 4 cognitive competencies), MemoryArena [He et al., 2026] (multi-session interdependent tasks; near-saturated LoCoMo models drop to 40-60%).

summary: As of September 2026, dual-memory architectures for AI agents have converged on neuroscience-inspired designs separating fast/episodic and slow/semantic memory systems, directly implementing Complementary Learning Systems (CLS) theory. Key advances span eight areas: (1) CLS theory provides the foundational hippocampal-neocortical mapping used by Dual-Layer Agentic Memory, Human-Inspired Architecture, HeLa-Mem, CraniMem, and others. (2) Episodic-semantic distinction is operationalized as dual stores (episodic buffer + knowledge graph) in CraniMem, SYNAPSE's unified graph with two node types, HeLa-Mem's dual graphs, and DG-Mem's exemplar/schema memories. (3) Consolidation/gating mechanisms include: Dual-Layer's small-to-large write routing + periodic write-back fine-tuning; Human-Inspired's sleep-phase consolidation + interference forgetting + maturation + reconsolidation; CraniMem's scheduled replay with utility scoring; HeLa-Mem's Hebbian Distillation; DG-Mem's reflection-store-mediated schema synthesis. (4) Dual-process cognitive models appear in D-Mem (System 1/2 with Quality Gating), Self-Evolving Agents framework, and DPE-Agent. (5) Dual-layer write routing is explicit in Dual-Layer Agentic Memory (fast routing cascade + slow consolidation) and Human-Inspired (ingestion → episodic → semantic). (6) Dual-grained memory with Shapley attribution is DG-Mem's core contribution — exemplar vs schema grains with Shapley value credit assignment for retrieval re-weighting. (7) Unified memory agents with RL include UMA (Task-Stratified GRPO), AgeMem (three-stage progressive RL + step-wise GRPO), Memory-R1, Mem-α, UMEM, MemFactory. (8) Dual-process with quality gating is D-Mem's Multi-dimensional Quality Gating (Relevance, Faithfulness, Completeness) achieving 96.7% of Full Deliberation performance at fraction of compute. The field has moved from static RAG to dynamic, consolidated, RL-optimized memory lifecycles with explicit gating, consolidation, and forgetting.
